endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Consider adding a required risk mitigation and monitoring plan in addition to the model card, especially for known risks specified on the model card.

endorsements.title: A Multidisciplinary Model for Risk Management and Detection of Ageist Bias in Healthcare Systems in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
endorsements.quote: Procurement should therefore pause or restrict deployment until adequate real-world geriatric data are collected.

commentary.bottom_line: No supplied study tests whether stopping or redirecting AI proposals at intake, when vendors cannot disclose or meet training-data demographic thresholds, changes which tools are adopted or how they perform for patients. The recommendation rests on one governance framework and one commentary, and no supplied study documents the hazard itself.

perspectives.view: Zero studies test the practice and zero studies document the hazard in this entry. The two endorsements are a framework playbook and a commentary, which GRADE treats as expert opinion rather than evidence. Certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence, and the effect of an intake gate on adoption or outcomes is unknown.

The commentary proposes pausing procurement until adequate geriatric data exist, and the CHAI playbook suggests a mitigation plan for risks listed on the model card. Neither source reports whether an intake gate catches unrepresentative tools before they reach patients, or how often a disclosed threshold predicts subgroup performance after deployment.

The CHAI language asks reviewers to consider a mitigation and monitoring plan, which is softer than a hard stop at intake. The recommendation goes further than its framework source by making nondisclosure a reason to halt review. No supplied study shows how vendors respond to such a requirement.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare health systems or procurement cycles with and without a demographic-representation gate at intake, measuring the share of proposals stopped, vendor disclosure rates, reviewer time, and subgroup model performance after deployment. Work is also needed to set threshold values and to test whether reported training-data composition predicts local performance for underrepresented groups.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. The only population named in the endorsements is older adults. Health systems serving these groups have no evidence on whether an intake threshold protects them or on which demographic categories and cutoffs a threshold should use.
